The present work attempted, for the first time, to apply a high preheating PBF-EB method to manufacture Ti-22Al25Nb alloy.
The microstructure and the tensile properties of the Ti-22Al25Nb alloy made by PBF-EB were investigated and compared with those made by the conventional PBF-LB process.
PBF-EB enabled the AM of the Ti-22Al-25 Nb alloy and indicated a unique microstructure, phase constitution, deformation behaviors, and excellent high-temperature tensile properties.
(1) The present study is the first to prepare Ti-22Al-25 Nb alloy using the PBF-EB system, which exhibited excellent high-temperature tensile strength, with a UTS of 803 MPa at 650°C.
In other words, the probability of O phase precipitating from β phase in PBF-EB sample was higher than that in PBF-LB, resulting in a more uniform microstructure in PBF-EB-manufactured materials.
(4) Two factors mainly affected the tensile properties of the PBF-LB and PBF-EB samples: the shape and quantity of the O phase and β phase, and dislocation density.
This study suggests the potential application of PBF-EB with a high preheating temperature for Ti-22Al-25 Nb fabrication.
Improving the metal vapor porosity in PBF-EB samples through subsequent heat treatment and optimizing process parameters is also a worthwhile area of investigation.

The molecular dynamics (MD) simulation method is one of the most powerful atomistic simulation methods used to study material properties, ranging from the atomic to the micro and even the mesoscale.
An MD package serves as the computational engine behind atomistic simulations, making it an essential tool for researchers in this field.
At that time, the package only supported the Lennard-Jones potential and its sole functionality was to calculate the thermal conductivity via the GreenKubo method.
